question: to the Council João Oliveira (The Left) Subject:

The Global Sumud flotilla, carrying humanitarian aid for Palestinians in the Gaza Strip, was attacked by Israeli military forces on 18 May 2026 around 463 km from the Gaza Strip. The attack 430 members of the flotilla being detained, including Portuguese nationals. Images have circulated showing soldiers beating, dragging, pushing and pinning down activists while Israeli minister Ben-Gvir shouts humiliating words at them. The same minister defended the assaults in the Israeli Parliament. Some members of the flotilla have reported acts of violence and physical, psychological and sexual torture. The way they were treated is unacceptable, indecent and inhumane. The attack and the assaults that followed form part of Israel’s systematic violation of international law, including the genocide of the Palestinian people in the Gaza Strip. The EU has an obligation to act to put an end to these atrocities. Staying silent and failing to speak up and condemn this state of affairs is, from a political or moral standpoint, not acceptable. In view of the above: 1.
Will the Council condemn Israel’s actions? What steps does it intend to take?
What measures will it adopt to ensure urgent humanitarian assistance reaches the Palestinian population in the Gaza Strip?
How does it justify maintaining the EU-Israel Association Agreement given the breaches of the Palestinian people’s rights and the crimes committed by the Israeli authorities?
